title: Patricia A. McCullough | Obituaries | rutlandherald.com
text:
Patricia A. (Gilman) McCullough PITTSFORD — Our beloved mother, Patricia Anne McCullough, passed on peacefully at home on October 29, 2026, after a long battle with heart and kidney failure. She was born on October 1, 1937, in Rutland, the daughter of Walter P. and Alice D. (McKirryher) Gilman. Patti attended Rutland City schools, and on November 6, 1954, she was crowned Queen of the Rutland Police Department’s first annual Ball. She graduated from Rutland High School in 1955. On November 24, 1956, she was married to William A. McCullough of Proctor, VT. They resided in Proctor until building their home in East Pittsford in 1960. She worked in local retail sales and manufacturing while raising her children and began working at General Electric when they were in their teenage years. She retired in 1996 after 25 years of service to care for Bill, who had suffered a debilitating stroke following surgery in 1994. Patti was an active senior and shared wonderful experiences with the local groups, traveling to luncheons, shows, dinners, concerts, and other outings. She enjoyed knitting, crocheting, cooking, coloring, and bird watching. Patti was predeceased by her parents; her infant son, Anthony, in 1965, her brother, Walter P. Gilman Jr., in 2000, and her husband in 2012. She is survived by her children: Timothy J. McCullough and his wife Margie of Leicester; William “Buzz” McCullough and his partner Kelly Carter of Pittsford; and Tammy Durgin and her husband Casey of Wallingford. In addition, she is survived by grandsons Troy, Trevor and Will McCullough, Colin Laramie, Zachary and Joshua Furman and his wife Sarah, and Jacob Durgin, as well as granddaughters Kelsey and Ashley McCullough, Kylyn Rocha, and Abigail Durgin, and 8 great-grandchildren. She also leaves behind her beloved feline buddy Youkilis, her faithful companion of 15 years; her best friend and traveling partner, Jeannette Bell; her loyal friends and neighbors who did much to help her stay in her home in recent years: Ken, Phyllis and Lee Smith, and Carol Calantas and Tom Squibb. In her final months, she was blessed to be surrounded by the loving care of her Visiting Nurses hospice team, Amy, Christine, MK, and Desiree, as well as Melissa, Makayla, Kaylee, and Nika of Ava’s Home Care. The family is eternally grateful for their compassion and support. Calling hours will be held on Friday, November 20, from 1–2 p.m. at Aldous Funeral Home in Rutland, followed by a service. The family will then receive guests to celebrate her life immediately thereafter, at a location to be announced. Her cremains will be laid to rest with her husband and son in Evergreen Cemetery, Pittsford, Vermont, at a private graveside service in the spring.
Patricia A. McCullough
